Computronium

01

Computronium: An Epistemic Laboratory for Learning

An open research framework for a governed, reproducible science of learning systems — not another catalogue of models.

  • The algorithm zoo is the problem. Hundreds of learning rules exist; almost none have been compared under equal budgets, equal architectures, and verified code.
  • A laboratory, not a library. Each experiment is one coordinate in a fixed ontology, run through a fixed pipeline, written to one ledger.
  • The bet. Learning mechanisms interact. The combinations that survive physical constraints are discoverable — if the instrument is honest.

The goal is not simply to build another model. It is to build the scientific instrument required to discover what makes learning systems work.

Open on the stakes, not on a feature list. The left of the diagram is the field as it is: a scatter of unreproducible experiments. The right is the claim of this project — a governed loop in which a run is a coordinate, an artifact is evidence, and a belief has to pass a gate.

State the promise explicitly: by the last slide the audience should know what this measures, what it refuses to claim, and how to join.

02

The Crisis of Comparison

Three failure modes, and one thing they have in common: the comparison is not the artifact.

  • Unequal tuning budgets. A published advantage is often a better hyperparameter sweep, not a better learning rule.
  • Unverified code. Every paper re-derives its baseline; a re-implementation defect reads as an algorithmic result.
  • The metric trap. One scalar hides the dynamics — stability, energy, memory, and plastic-state capacity trade against accuracy.

What is missing is not another algorithm. It is a fair way to compare them.

Artifact of the comparison What it silently encodes
architecture and width inductive bias
seed count and selection rule variance budget
hyperparameter prior the author's tuning effort
the reported metric which trade-off is allowed to hide

Frame this as infrastructure, not accusation: individual papers are usually careful, the field has no shared instrument.

Walk the table left to right. Each row is a degree of freedom a comparison must declare before it is legal. The fairness contract in the closing slide is the answer to this table, clause by clause.

03

The 6-Axis Ontology

System = Substrate × Geometry × StateDynamics × Plasticity × CreditAssignment × ParameterUpdate

Every experiment is a coordinate. Change one axis, hold five constant, and the comparison isolates one mechanism instead of confounding six.

Axis Symbol Question it answers Primitives
Substrate S physical state space: precision, noise, sparsity 9
Geometry G topology and routing of computational units 11
Dynamics D forward evolution and settling — the "forward pass" 8
Plasticity P what becomes a dynamical variable inside an episode 7
Credit C how error is routed and pseudo-gradients are computed 10
Update U slow, persistent consolidation of parameters 12

SystemConfig.validate() whitelists legal combinations, so the compatible region — not the full Cartesian product — is the search space. The decomposition is a design abstraction, not a law of computation: a five-dimensional system is the P = NullPlasticity subspace.

Do not oversell the ontology as physics. It earns its keep only if it makes comparisons legal, and that is an engineering claim: validation whitelists what composes.

Point at the highlighted polygon: this is one system. The dotted hexagon is the inner ring at half scale — a reference grid, not a score. The counts in the table are read from the registries at build time; today they total 57 available primitives.

04

Beyond Backpropagation

64 carded implementations — 43 primitives and 21 composed algorithms — each with an identity card: reference, declared deviations, objective, pseudo-gradient, and symmetry.

The kernel ladder

An implementation earns its rung. Nothing starts verified.

Rung Count What the rung asserts
reference_only 39 readable, tested semantics; no accelerated path
kernel_unverified 20 a kernel exists; parity is not yet proven
kernel_verified 5 parity against the reference plus a micro-benchmark

At the top rung today:

Implementation Axis Kernel
credit_assignment.local_goodness credit assignment triton
credit_assignment.random_projections credit assignment triton
state_dynamics.energy_minimization state dynamics torch_compile
state_dynamics.predictive_settling state dynamics torch_compile
algorithm.backprop torch_compile

The top rung is deliberately small. The large reference_only count is the honest state of the art, published rather than hidden: a scientific record needs the slow, readable implementation more than it needs a fast unverified one.

The ladder is the answer to "why should I trust the fast path". A rung is a claim with a test behind it: parity to the reference implementation, then a micro-benchmark that proves the kernel is worth dispatching.

If asked why so few are verified: because verification is ranked by use, and an unverified kernel is still a documented, runnable system. Say the number out loud rather than implying everything is optimized.

05

From Question to Governed Evidence

from computronium.experiment.schema.seed_registries import seed_all_registries
from computronium.experiment.surface.profiles import question_first

seed_all_registries()
spec = question_first(
    "validation_accuracy", "mnist",
    {"budget_seconds": 600, "fidelity": "L1", "n_seeds": 3},
)

spec is a RunSpec: the objective, the declared operating point, and the canonical stage list. No hidden default escapes into a result.

11 stages, none skippable

  • S1–S4 define — frame the question, generate the search space, schedule fidelities, gate legality.
  • S5–S8 execute — compose the coordinate, train at increasing fidelity, measure, record.
  • S9–S11 judge — attribute variance, decide promotion, report.

Every run writes one record (19 fields, schema v3) to an append-only DuckDB ledger through 12 store methods. No silent drops, no lost seeds.

The code is the whole entry point: an objective, a task, an operating point. The operating point is the fairness contract made executable — budget, fidelity, seed count are declared before a number exists.

Stress S4: the legality gate rejects a coordinate that the ontology does not compose, which is where most "surprising" results would have been caught. S8 is append-only so a failed seed stays in the record.

06

An Instrument, Not a Picture

  • Real-time telemetry. FastAPI and WebSockets stream the campaign queue, cell state, and resource utilisation while the run is live.
  • A control plane. Play, pause, step, and move the compute ceiling mid-flight. The campaign is steerable, not launched and abandoned.
  • Mission control. Pareto views over 48 registered objectives — 41 of them actually measured — so accuracy never gets to stand alone.

The screenshot is captured from a real campaign by scripts/capture_dashboard_tour.py, not mocked. Panels shown are the live rail, the Pareto plot, and the control bar.

The point of the dashboard is auditing during the run: when a cell is promoted, the panel shows which cells it beat and under which budget. Do not demo the animation; demo a pause and a reallocation.

07

Trustworthy Results: the Epistemic Ledger

Three objects are routinely confused in the literature. Here they are separate, and separately addressable.

  • Measurement — a number with provenance: which run, which seed, which artifact produced it.
  • Claim — a statement over a declared scope, derived from measurements.
  • Gated belief — a claim that passed its checks. A belief can lose its gate and re-enter as evidence.

Claims are property-tested, not asserted: Lyapunov descent for energy-based dynamics, gradient equivalence between each credit rule and its reference, finite-state invariants for plasticity mechanisms.

This is the differentiator. Lead with the distinction between a number and a belief: most dashboards stop at the left of the chain.

The loop at the bottom matters — a gate is not a one-way promotion. When a later campaign contradicts a belief, the belief is revoked and the evidence stays. Point at docs/CORRECTIONS.md as the public memory of that.

08

The Research Horizon

Stability versus plasticity

The frontier itself is the object of study: spectral radius and Lyapunov exponents on one axis, adaptation speed on the other. A system that is only fast is not a result.

The resource vector

C = (compute, memory, energy, latency, plastic-state capacity)

Reported per run. Never collapsed into a scalar, because the collapse is where physical constraints get to hide.

Physics-ready by construction

Local credit, explicit settling, and energy terms are ontology-level constraints, not retrofits. Substrates available today: digital, analog, memristive, neuromorphic, optical, quantum, complex, sparse, ternary.

No physical-hardware superiority is claimed. Neuromorphic, memristive, and photonic paths are validated in simulation until they run on silicon.

The trade-off is the deep question: stability without adaptation is a frozen model, adaptation without stability is a system that forgets. The instrument's job is to place each system on the frontier with error bars.

Be explicit about the simulation caveat. The substrate axis exists so that locality and energy are first-class from the start; it does not yet prove anything about a device.

09

The Invitation: an Evaluation Consortium

A consortium needs three shared artifacts, and none of them is a model.

  • A fairness contract — 6 clauses that make a comparison legal before it is run. docs/FAIRNESS_CONTRACT.md
  • Identity cards — 31 cards declaring reference, deviations, objective, pseudo-gradient, and symmetry; the admission ticket for a new algorithm. docs/IDENTITY_CARDS.md
  • A corrections log — 5 public entries recording what failed, why, and what changed. docs/CORRECTIONS.md

uv run comp --help is the instrument itself.

The goal is not simply to build another model. It is to build the scientific instrument required to discover what makes learning systems work.

Close on the ask, not on the architecture: bring one algorithm, card it, and let the contract compare it. The deposit is a YAML identity card and a run under a declared operating point.

End on the closing line, then stop. Offer the repository and a concrete next step — card an algorithm you already trust, and we will publish whether it survives.
